angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 534,993 km at 126.66 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.8953 +/- 0.0306 mas (same row, RUWE 1.66): 126.66 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.769 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Rodriguez et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1811 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.521.2765R/abstract): 534,993 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.817 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Rodriguez et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1811 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.521.2765R/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4766 +/- 52 K from Rodriguez et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1811 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.521.2765R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Rodriguez et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1811 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.521.2765R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1811.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.578, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1811 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.306 dex, from Rodriguez et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.521.2765R/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1811 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.56019, from Rodriguez et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.521.2765R/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1811 (pscomppars): age 5.9 Gyr, from Rodriguez et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.521.2765R/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
